env:
A stock RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell host with two GPUs, Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC credentials, and the VSS repository at `{{repo_root}}`. The prompts are verbatim from the VDR slide. Query 1 stands a deployment up; query 2 extends it.

Write query 1's artifacts under `_builds/vdr-2-base/` and query 2's under `_builds/vdr-2-alerting-summarization/`. For both, bring the stack up with a detached `docker compose ... up -d` from the validated `resolved.yml` as soon as validation passes. No agent harness: answer the harness question with no - the developer drives the build from their own coding agent with the `vss` CLI.

expects.query: deploy a vss vision agent, non-interactively
checks: `sh -c 'cd {{repo_root}} && export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vss-judge-venv" && uv run --project libs/vss vss --version >/dev/null 2>&1; i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do uv run --project libs/vss vss configure --base-url http://localhost:7777 >/dev/null 2>&1 && c=$(uv run --project libs/vss vss configure check 2>/dev/null) && echo "$c" | grep -Eq "^ *vlm +available" && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (a fresh `vss configure` against the compose edge proxy `vss-haproxy-ingress` at `:7777`, then `vss configure check` exiting 0 - every recorded route answers its live re-probe - with the `vlm` command group reported available: the base profile's integrated RT-VLM routed and serving; polls up to ~2 min after a one-off venv warm-up). The judge's `uv run` uses its own environment (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`), so a `.venv` the agent left in the checkout - built against another interpreter - cannot fail this check.
`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do docker ps --format "{{.Names}}" | grep -qx vss-agent-ui && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (Web UI; polls up to ~2 min).
`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do docker ps --format "{{.Names}}" | grep -qx vss-rtvi-vlm && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (integrated RT-VLM; polls up to ~2 min).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | awk '$0 == "vss-agent" { found=1 } END { exit found ? 1 : 0 }'` returns exit 0 (the in-stack agent is absent, as the harness choice requires).

expects.query: take down the vision agent and add vlm alerting and video summarization to my deployment
checks: `sh -c 'cd {{repo_root}} && export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vss-judge-venv" && uv run --project libs/vss vss --version >/dev/null 2>&1; i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do uv run --project libs/vss vss configure --base-url http://localhost:7777 >/dev/null 2>&1 && c=$(uv run --project libs/vss vss configure check 2>/dev/null) && echo "$c" | grep -Eq "^ *summarize +available" && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (a fresh `vss configure`, then `vss configure check` exiting 0 - every recorded route answers its live re-probe - with the `summarize` command group reported available: the LVS route served through the edge proxy; polls up to ~2 min after a one-off venv warm-up). The judge's `uv run` uses its own environment (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`), so a `.venv` the agent left in the checkout - built against another interpreter - cannot fail this check.

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do docker ps --format "{{.Names}}" | grep -qx vss-alert-bridge && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (real-time VLM alerting; polls up to ~2 min).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:7777/alert-bridge/health >/dev/null && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (Alert Bridge answers its health route through the edge proxy, not merely a running container; polls up to ~2 min).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do k=$(docker inspect -f "{{.State.Health.Status}}" kafka 2>/dev/null); [ "$k" = healthy ] && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (the Kafka broker Alert Bridge publishes VLM alerts to is healthy; polls up to ~2 min).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do k=$(docker inspect -f "{{.State.Health.Status}}" elasticsearch 2>/dev/null); [ "$k" = healthy ] && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (the Elasticsearch store alerts are indexed into is healthy; polls up to ~2 min).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 36 ]; do s=$(docker inspect -f "{{if .State.Health}}{{.State.Health.Status}}{{else}}{{.State.Status}}{{end}}" vss-lvs 2>/dev/null); [ "$s" = healthy ] || [ "$s" = running ] && exit 0; sleep 10; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (LVS up: its compose healthcheck (`/v1/ready`, probed by Docker) when the build defines one, else simply running - a build whose LVS carries no healthcheck must not fail on the absence of one. Readiness proper is the `summarize available` check above; this one localises a failure to the container. Model warm-up can take minutes, so polls up to ~6 min).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do docker ps --format "{{.Names}}" | grep -qx vss-video-analytics-api && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (analytics REST API; polls up to ~2 min).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do docker ps --format "{{.Names}}" | grep -qx vss-rtvi-vlm && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (RT-VLM still serving after the rebuild; polls up to ~2 min).

`sh -c 'e=$(docker inspect -f "{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}" vss-agent-ui) && for k in NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_CHAT_SIDEBAR NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_CHAT_TAB NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_SEARCH_TAB; do printf "%s\n" "$e" | grep -qx "$k=false" || exit 1; done'` returns exit 0 (the running Web UI hides the chat sidebar, Chat tab and Search tab: with no harness nothing answers them).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | awk '$0 == "vss-agent" { found=1 } END { exit found ? 1 : 0 }'` returns exit 0 (the build remains harness-free after the rebuild).
